title: Analysis of Lignin Derived Products Using UHPLC-MS/MS-DAD
author: Kelsey J. Ramirez
materials: Agilent Quantitative Analysis for QQQ version 12.1

steps.title: Prepare individual stock standards
steps.instruction: Weigh each analyte to the desired concentration and dissolve it in the specified diluent listed for that compound.

substeps.instruction: Terephthalic acid – dissolve in the diluent described in the referenced protocol.
Phthalic acid – dissolve in 18.2 MΩ·cm ultrapure water (UPW) and ethanol.
Benzoic acid – dissolve in ethanol.
Isophthalic acid – dissolve in dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO).
Biphenyl‑3,3‑dicarboxylic acid – dissolve in DMSO.
Protocatechuic acid – dissolve in ethanol.
Catechol – dissolve in ethanol.
cis,cis‑muconic acid – dissolve in 0.05 % v/v sodium hydroxide.
cis,trans‑muconic acid – dissolve in 0.05 % v/v sodium hydroxide (see referenced preparation protocol).
1,2,4‑Benzenetricarboxylic acid – dissolve in ethanol.
1,2,3‑Benzenetricarboxylic acid (Hemimellitic acid) – dissolve in ethanol.
1,3,5‑Benzenetricarboxylic acid (Trimesic acid) – dissolve in ethanol.
Muconolactone – dissolve in M9 minimal media (compound synthesized in‑house, purity > 99 % verified by NMR).

steps.title: Create mixed standard working solutions
steps.instruction: Combine the individual stock solutions according to the mixed standard working solution (MSWS) table, keeping TPA, cis,cis‑muconic acid, cis,trans‑muconic acid, and muconolactone as separate standards.

substeps.instruction: Refer to the provided MSWS table for the exact volumes/compositions.
Do not mix TPA, cis,cis‑muconic acid, cis,trans‑muconic acid, or muconolactone with other analytes because of isomerization, solvent compatibility, and solubility issues.

steps.title: Prepare calibration curves
steps.instruction: Using the MSWS, generate calibration standards covering the method range of 1 µg/mL to 500 µg/mL with at least five calibration points, then filter all samples before analysis.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the MSWS with the appropriate diluent to create at least five calibration points spanning 1–500 µg/mL (example scheme provides nine points).
Select the linear range that gives the best analyte response and instrument performance.
Filter every calibration standard and unknown sample through a 0.2 µm filter prior to injection.
If any sample is expected to fall outside the 1–500 µg/mL range, dilute it appropriately to avoid carry‑over or system contamination.

steps.title: Set up UHPLC system
steps.instruction: Configure the Agilent 1290 UHPLC system with the defined method parameters for a total run time of 7.0 minutes, including the UHPLC, DAD, and multi‑wash settings.

substeps.instruction: Load the UHPLC method file containing the specified gradient, flow rate, column temperature, and detector wavelengths.
Set the total run time to 7.0 minutes.
Apply the defined DAD parameters and multi‑wash program as provided.

steps.title: Run UHPLC‑MS/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the filtered samples on an Agilent 6475 triple‑quadrupole mass spectrometer with dual Agilent jet‑stream electrospray ionization (AJS ESI) using the defined source and MS/MS parameters.

substeps.instruction: Load the source method file with the illustrated AJS ESI settings.
Apply the defined MS/MS parameters (fragmentor voltages, collision energies, etc.).
For muconolactone, use the provided MRM transitions, fragmentor voltages, and collision energies for quantifying and qualifying ions.
For all other analytes, use the DAD wavelengths listed in the provided table.
Inject each sample according to the UHPLC method and acquire data.

steps.title: Process data
steps.instruction: Analyze the acquired data using Agilent Quantitative Analysis for QQQ software version 12.1 Update 1.

steps.title: Perform quality control checks
steps.instruction: Validate instrument performance and data quality throughout the run using calibration and verification criteria.

substeps.instruction: Ensure each calibration curve has a correlation coefficient (r²) ≥ 0.995 (linear or quadratic fit).
Run a calibration verification standard (CVS) taken from the calibration curve after every ≤20 samples to monitor drift.
Accept CVS recoveries only if they fall within ±15 % of the expected amount.
